claim: For every integer \(n\ge0\), the exact harmonic orbit \(\gamma(t)=(\cos t,-\sin t)\) of the Adjaï–Akande–Yehossou–Monsia family \(\ddot x+x(\dot x^2+\dot x\sum_{\ell=0}^{n}x^{2\ell}+x^2-1)\dot x+x^{2n+3}=0\) has both planar Floquet multipliers exactly equal to \(1\). With \(R=x^2+y^2-1\) and \(S_n(x)=\sum_{\ell=0}^{n}x^{2\ell}\), the full planar system satisfies the exact defect law \(\dot R=-2xy(y+S_n(x))R\); the normal period exponent on the unit circle is zero. Hence the harmonic cycle is nonhyperbolic for every \(n\ge0\) and cannot be exponentially attracting or repelling. The claim does not determine isolation, semistability, a surrounding periodic annulus, or higher-order nonlinear stability.

correctness.rationale: Starting from the printed equation, direct algebra gives the exact multiplicative defect equation for \(R\). Along the exact unit circle, the normal exponent splits into a closed one-variable integral and \(\int_0^{2\pi}\cos t\sin^2t\,dt\), both exactly zero. Planar Floquet/Liouville theory then gives transverse multiplier \(1\), while autonomy gives the tangential multiplier \(1\). The finite checker is corroborative only; the proof quantifies over all integers \(n\ge0\).

value.rationale: The paper deliberately constructs infinitely many polynomial oscillators of growing degree around the same exact harmonic cycle and motivates them as exact nonlinear benchmarks. The transverse Floquet multiplier is the canonical local robustness/stability invariant of such a cycle. Showing it is identically \(1\) for every family member exposes an exact structural degeneracy that phase portraits do not reveal: none of these cycles is hyperbolic or exponentially attracting/repelling. That is a mathematically motivated boundary fact, not a cosmetic recomputation.
